discovery: Discovery of neutron halo nuclei and the opening of the physics of nuclei far from stability

nominees.name: Isao Tanihata
nominees.affiliation: RCNP, Osaka University, Japan / Beihang University, China

motivation: In 1985 Isao Tanihata, using radioactive-beam interaction cross-section measurements at Berkeley, found that 11Li has an anomalously large matter radius. Björn Jonson, with the late P. G. Hansen, explained it in 1987: the weakly bound valence neutrons form a dilute 'halo' that extends far beyond the core. This combination of precise experiment and clear physical insight overturned the textbook picture of nuclei as compact, constant-density drops. It showed that nuclear shell structure and symmetries change far from stability, and it revealed Borromean three-body binding and new collective modes. These results gave rise to radioactive-beam facilities around the world, including RIKEN, GANIL, FAIR and FRIB. They also link nuclear structure to few-body quantum physics, Efimov-like phenomena and the r-process synthesis of heavy elements. Few discoveries have so deeply transformed how we understand the atomic nucleus.
